blocks.text: compose.override.yaml is merged automatically; explicit `-f` stacks replace that default; profiles make services optional.

$ docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.prod.yaml up -d      # override file NOT loaded
$ docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.prod.yaml config     # inspect the merge

rows: Combined, so omission can't remove entries

items: Remove or replace inherited sequences with `!reset []` / `!override` (recent Compose), or keep them out of the base file.
`include:` imports self-contained sub-projects, cleaner than long -f stacks.

blocks.text:
$ docker compose --profile tools up -d
$ COMPOSE_PROFILES=local-llm docker compose up -d
Services without profiles always run; a profiled service runs if its profile is active or it's targeted explicitly.

Q: "How do you keep dev and prod Compose config apart?" A: "A prod-like base compose.yaml, dev ergonomics (bind mounts, --reload, debug ports) in compose.override.yaml, prod limits and restart policies in compose.prod.yaml loaded with -f (which skips the override), and profiles for optional tooling. Sequences merge, so use !reset to drop dev ports."
